hook: Paul Christiano holds a PhD in statistical learning theory from UC Berkeley. While working on the alignment team at OpenAI, he was a co-author and principal architect of the 2017 paper Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences, which introduced the technique now known as reinforcement learning from human feedback, using human comparisons between possible outputs to train reinforcement learning systems. That approach was later adapted to fine-tune large language models and became a standard part of how systems like ChatGPT are trained to follow instructions and match human judgment. In 2021 he left OpenAI to found the Alignment Research Center (ARC), a nonprofit that develops theoretical and empirical methods for understanding and evaluating advanced AI systems, including work on eliciting latent knowledge from neural networks. He was named to the Time 100 Most Influential People in AI in 2023, and in 2024 he began advising the U.S. government's AI safety evaluation work through what is now NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation.
